name: Wirt Sikes
knownFor: American journalist and consul whose British Goblins gathered Welsh folklore and customs.

works.title: A Book for the Winter-Evening Fireside
British Goblins: Welsh Folk-Lore, Fairy Mythology, Legends and Traditions
Rambles and Studies in Old South Wales

events.text: Working as a typesetter and contributor at the Utica Morning Herald.
Became canal inspector in Chicago for the state-owned Illinois and Michigan Canal.
Married the lecturer Olive Logan; they went to Europe and kept up their journalism there.
Appointed United States Consul at Cardiff, Wales.
Published British Goblins, from the pieces on Welsh folklore, mythology and customs he wrote during his consulship.
Died at Brompton and was buried in Brookwood Cemetery, Surrey.

relevance: British Goblins is the book that brought together Welsh fairy lore, legends and customs for English-language readers. Sikes was not a trained folklorist but a working journalist with an interest in the people he met as consul, and the book shows both the reach and the limits of that approach.
influence: He is best remembered today for his writings on Welsh folklore and customs. He is also said to have used as many as thirty pseudonyms across a prolific, mostly forgotten output.
